title: July's Demand Gen Drop adds Checkout Links in nine markets and upgraded tROAS
summary: Google's July Demand Gen Drop expands Checkout Links to nine new markets (incl. Australia, France, Mexico, South Korea) and upgrades Target ROAS bidding so campaigns are less cautious early and reach targets faster. It also pushes product-feed integration, affiliate partnerships boost, and YouTube checkout links / Universal Commerce Protocol (US only) ahead of the holiday season.

title: Google documents text disclaimer assets for Search ads
summary: Google published Help Center guidance for text disclaimer assets, which put required legal terms inside Search ads. They are available to all advertisers worldwide, added after campaign creation via the Assets menu, capped at 90 characters, and compatible with AI Max. Disapproved disclaimers do not stop the ad serving, but a disclaimer asset overrides a pinned Description Line 1 and may be truncated.

title: Google publishes its first dedicated guide for YouTube audio ads
summary: Google released a standalone help page for YouTube audio ads, consolidating specs and setup: upload a video (static image or simple animation), where creative up to 15s serves non-skippable and 16–30s serves skippable, built under the Brand awareness and reach objective using the Audio video subtype with Target CPM. No new product — it makes the format easier to set up correctly.

title: Google Analytics flags campaigns missing GBRAID and gad_ identifiers
summary: Google Analytics added a diagnostic that flags landing-page URLs where aggregate identifiers such as GBRAID and gad_ are missing, and explains how to fix them. Missing parameters degrade campaign attribution accuracy, so the alert helps catch measurement gaps before they distort reporting.

title: Structured Data Files v10.1 lands for DV360; pre-v10 versions deprecated
summary: SDF v10.1 is generally available for Display & Video 360, adding a field to declare whether a YouTube asset was created or edited with AI, DOOH insertion order and line item support, new columns mapping creatives to ads and ad groups, and updated Inventory Mode values. All SDF versions before v10 are deprecated, so bulk-management workflows need to migrate.

title: Google extends its AI-generated ad description test to Shopping ads
summary: AI-generated descriptions have been spotted alongside Shopping and Product ads, extending an experiment Google confirmed on Search ads earlier in July. The copy is generated by Google rather than the advertiser, so Shopping advertisers who tune titles and descriptions now have messaging in the SERP they do not directly control.

title: Google rolls out AI content labels for ad creatives across its ad platforms
summary: Advertisers can now label image and video assets as AI-generated or AI-edited, via per-asset labels or a new AI label setting rolling out across Google Ads, DV360, Campaign Manager 360, Merchant Center and Ads Editor. A new AI Label column shows whether labelling is on, and labelled assets show an AI disclosure icon. Google may auto-label assets made with its own AI tools, and warns the setting alone does not guarantee compliance with EU, India or New York rules.

title: Target CPA and Target ROAS now appear as standalone bidding strategies
summary: Google Ads is surfacing Target CPA and Target ROAS as their own bidding strategies in campaign setup instead of optional targets inside Maximize Conversions / Maximize Conversion Value. Mechanics appear unchanged, but the layout may be groundwork for the bidding changes scheduled for August 17.

title: Policy certifications move into the Google Ads account
summary: Starting in August, eligible advertisers can submit Social Casino Games certification requests from a new Policy > Account section under Admin instead of the Help Center, with a copyrighted-content certification form also spotted. Existing certifications and pending applications are unaffected; accounts without access keep using the Help Center flow.

title: Google Ads Editor 2.13 adds AI Max for Shopping and PMax retention goals
summary: Editor 2.13 brings full AI Max support to Shopping campaigns (automated text generation, URL expansion controls, brand lists, URL exclusions), Customer Retention Goals for Performance Max, Business Name/Logo fields for responsive and non-skippable video, Maps placement for Demand Gen, Native Channel Performance reporting, and a User Attestation field for AI disclosure. Creating new Video Action campaigns is retired.

title: Household income exclusions surface in Performance Max
summary: A campaign-level setting spotted in a European PMax campaign lets advertisers exclude Google's estimated household income brackets — top 10%, 11–20%, 21–30%, 31–40%, 41–50%, lower 50%, and unknown. It would be one of the few real audience controls in PMax, useful for luxury, finance and premium services (or the inverse for value brands).

title: AI Max appears in Standard Shopping campaigns
summary: AI Max is rolling out to Standard Shopping: AI matching to conversational long-tail queries, ad copy auto-generated from Merchant Center feed attributes, Final URL Expansion that can send traffic to a different landing page, and Google choosing between a Shopping ad or a text ad per query. Campaign-level controls cover asset optimization, brand exclusions and turning Final URL Expansion off; existing bidding and targeting stay in place.

title: Google Ads API v25 adds YouTube sub-format reporting and a loyalty retention goal
summary: v25 adds an ad_sub_format_type segment splitting non-skippable in-stream YouTube ads by duration, comments/likes/shares for Shorts ads, a loyalty retention goal with bid adjustments and PLA member benefits, migration of new-customer-acquisition goals to the unified goals framework, and richer YouTube creator insights. Client libraries and code must be upgraded.

title: Video campaign groups roll out globally for YouTube reach and frequency
summary: Advertisers can now group multiple YouTube reach-and-frequency campaigns under one shared reach or frequency goal while keeping per-campaign budgets, creative and settings, with unified reporting on unique reach and average weekly impressions. Google cites a Meridian MMM study putting optimal frequency at 2.7 impressions/week for a 19% ROI lift.

title: Missed growth estimates move into the Recommendations tab as a beta
summary: The Missed Growth Opportunity insight graduates from Google Ads Labs into the Recommendations tab for eligible accounts, estimating clicks, conversions and conversion value lost to limited budgets or low bids and attributing the cause to one or the other. The figures are modelled estimates, not guarantees.

title: Google Ads adds bulk linking of accounts to a GA4 property
summary: A new bulk option under Data Manager > Google Analytics 4 > Link Setup lets advertisers select or deselect multiple Google Ads accounts for one GA4 property instead of linking each account individually — useful for agencies, franchises and enterprise teams keeping measurement consistent as accounts change.

title: Google drops the $50K spend requirement for Lead Form assets
summary: Google's Help documentation no longer lists the $50,000 lifetime Google Ads spend threshold for Lead Form assets; the only remaining eligibility path is the advertiser-reputation route ($1,000 per account or $15,000 across accounts plus Advertiser Verification). Campaign support for Lead Form assets was also simplified, opening Google-hosted lead gen to far smaller advertisers.

title: Google Tag Manager adds guided setup for Google Ads purchase conversions
summary: A new Guided Setup card in Google Tag Manager automatically creates the tags, triggers and variables needed for Google Ads purchase conversion tracking instead of requiring manual configuration. It is in beta and not yet available to all GTM users, but should reduce setup errors that feed bad data into automated bidding.

title: Enhanced Brand Lift studies detect lifts as low as 1.2% — at 3x the budget
summary: Google Ads now offers a choice between Standard Brand Lift (measures lifts of 2%+) and Enhanced Brand Lift (detects lifts from 1.2%). Google says the enhanced option needs roughly three times the budget but raises the chance of detecting a positive lift by 60%, making it practical mainly for larger upper-funnel campaigns.

title: PMax alpha lets selected advertisers turn off Search Partners and Display
summary: Google is running a limited alpha in which selected Performance Max advertisers get two campaign-level checkboxes — on by default — to deselect the Search Partner Network and the Google Display Network, inventory that was previously compulsory. Google confirmed it is a pilot with no timeline for broader availability; several agencies said their access requests were refused, while others found the checkboxes with no notification.

title: Google to recognise LegitScript certification for Spanish telemedicine ads from Aug. 5
summary: From August 5, 2026, Google will accept LegitScript Healthcare Certification as the compliance route for telemedicine providers advertising in Spain — a category that previously had no compliant path onto Google search and display inventory. Spain becomes the eleventh market where the certification gates healthcare advertising.

title: Crypto exchange and wallet ads open in Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein
summary: A July 22 Advertising Policies change-log update extends Google's crypto advertising framework to the three non-EU EEA states from August 2026, covering exchanges plus software and hardware wallets. Advertisers must hold a MiCA Crypto-Asset Service Provider licence from a national authority, meet local requirements, and be Google-certified.

title: Google Ads ends in-account appeals for policy decisions older than 6 months
summary: Effective July 21, 2026 — published and enforced the same day, with no notice period — advertisers can no longer appeal a Google Ads policy decision from inside the account if the decision is more than six months old. The change was documented only in the Advertising Policies change log, and is retroactive in effect for accounts actioned before that window.

title: Local Services Ads fold into Google Ads as pay-per-lead PMax; historical reports are lost
summary: From August 2026 Google retires the standalone Local Services Ads dashboard and converts LSA campaigns into a Performance Max campaign type with pay-per-lead goals, starting with US home and storefront service advertisers and rolling account-by-account. Pay-per-lead billing and Search/Maps-only placement stay; manual bidding ends and past performance reports are not carried over, so advertisers must export them before their transition date.

title: Google says its August 17 Smart Bidding change is narrower than advertisers fear
summary: Ahead of the August 17, 2026 bidding change, Google repeated that the update touches only campaigns carrying a 'Limited by budget' status, pushing back on a widespread belief in the PPC community that a broader Smart Bidding overhaul is being shipped under a narrow label. Advertisers with budget-constrained campaigns should expect delivery changes on that date.

title: Microsoft Advertising brings Ad Preview Hub to Performance Max
summary: Ad Preview Hub, previously limited to Audience Ads, is now in Microsoft Advertising Performance Max campaigns. Open an asset group, choose Preview ads, and review eligible formats across devices and placements, then generate a secure shareable link so clients and stakeholders can approve creative without account access.

title: Microsoft retires Predictive Matching and folds it into AI Max search term matching
summary: Microsoft Advertising confirmed — via a notice inserted into help documents including the keyword match types page, with no blog post — that Predictive Matching is being retired and moved to Search term matching within AI Max. Microsoft says no action is required and gave no effective date, so advertisers who relied on the feature have no timeline for the switch.

title: Graph/Marketing API v26.0 blocks 47 commerce endpoints and drops Explore Feed and poll ads
summary: Effective July 29, 2026, Meta blocked 47 Commerce Order Management endpoints (order listing, shipment tracking, refunds, tax settings) with no replacement API, as the Shops checkout infrastructure is retired. The same release removes the Instagram Explore Feed ad placement, strips Messenger Stories from targeting, and blocks creating new poll ad creatives. Restrictions extend to all remaining API versions on October 27, 2026.

title: Meta opens its ads MCP server to any developer app
summary: Meta's ads Model Context Protocol server, announced July 16, is now available to any developer holding a Meta app rather than only Meta's own connectors, removing the custom integration code previously required to connect AI agents to Meta ads. Agents can create and edit campaigns, ad sets and ads, manage Custom Audiences and catalogs, and query spend, impressions, CTR and ROAS through natural language.

title: TikTok's Q3 product preview adds TopView regional exclusions and TopReach Max Reach
summary: TikTok's third 2026 quarterly product preview (July 28) bundles eight sets of ad changes across reservation buys, catalog automation, commerce bidding, contextual inventory, generative creative and agent tooling. The most concrete lever for buyers: national TopView campaigns can now exclude up to 40% of a market's sub-regions. It also introduces TopReach Max Reach, combining TopView and TopFeed into one automated unique-reach buy with age, gender and interest targeting.

title: Safari 27 beta blocks Bing UET at the network layer and restricts the LinkedIn Insight Tag
summary: A WebKit source review by analytics engineer Mariusz Brucki found Safari 27's developer beta adds IP-level blocking that terminates outbound connections to ad servers regardless of the script's domain. Bing's UET endpoint (bat.bing.com) resolves into a blocked Microsoft ad-infrastructure IP range, and the LinkedIn Insight Tag (snap.licdn.com) is classified for fingerprinting restrictions that strip URL query parameters and referrer data. Findings come from the beta source, not Apple's release notes.

title: LinkedIn Campaign Manager adds Draft with AI, Brand Kit and Ad Variants
summary: LinkedIn introduced AI-powered creative tooling in Campaign Manager: AI ad-copy generation, a Brand Kit for consistent brand assets, a new 'Flexible' campaign creation flow, and Ad Variants that generate multiple versions of an existing ad with alternative headlines and intro text. Surfaced via SocialBee's July 2026 LinkedIn roundup.
